title: Zelensky replaces commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskyi with Mykhailo Drapatyi
body:
On 21 July 2026, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky dismissed four-star General Oleksandr Syrskyi as commander-in-chief of the armed forces and appointed Major General Mykhailo Drapatyi in his place, according to Euronews. The decision followed days of mass protests that began after Zelensky dismissed Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who had served about six months. Critics said Zelensky had sided with Syrskyi in the dispute.

Zelensky credited Syrskyi with Ukraine's successes in the defence of Kyiv, the Kharkiv offensive and the Kursk operation. Syrskyi wrote on Facebook that he was handing over an army "on the offensive" and said he would keep serving Ukraine in some capacity.

Drapatyi had led the Joint Forces command covering the Kharkiv front from autumn 2025, when Ukrainian units recaptured territory around Kupiansk. Earlier he led the Dnipro operational-strategic group, which Syrskyi dissolved in October 2025. In 2014, as a major and battalion commander in the 72nd Mechanised Brigade, he fought in the battle for Mariupol.

Protest organiser Dmytro Koziatynskyi demanded Syrskyi's dismissal and Fedorov's reinstatement, and set a deadline of 24 July 2026, after which he threatened an indefinite protest. Zelensky had not commented on whether Fedorov would return to the post.
